variants: Sum Insured; applied Sum; Cover Amount; Final Sum
definition: The total guaranteed benefit amount of life insurance coverage applied for or approved under a policy.
note: While 'applied Sum' refers to the requested amount and 'Final Sum' to the approved amount, they represent stages of the same core coverage concept.

variants: Meridian Life; Assurance Ltd; Life Assurance
definition: The primary insurance company issuing the life insurance policies.
note: Settled by using the full corporate name inferred from references to Meridian Life and Assurance Ltd.

definition: The professional reinsurance company that accepts risks exceeding the primary insurer's retention limit.

variants: aggregate EM; aggregate extra; Cr Rated-up
definition: The elevated mortality risk of an applicant compared to standard lives, expressed as a percentage loading for premium calculations.
note: EM stands for Extra Mortality. 'Cr Rated-up' refers to the underwriting decision to load the premium due to this extra risk.

variants: Examination Details; Full Medicals; Medical Exam Details
definition: A physical assessment of an applicant's health conducted by a qualified medical professional to gather underwriting evidence.
The official document containing clinical findings and measurements compiled by the visiting or examining doctor.
The evaluation of an applicant's financial status, income, and net worth to ensure the requested coverage aligns with their economic value.
The process of evaluating an applicant's medical history, physical exams, and lab test results to assess mortality risk.
The maximum amount of risk or sum assured that the insurer is willing to keep on its own books without ceding to a reinsurer.

variants: reinsurer referral; Referral Raised; Referral Response; Response Received
definition: The process of sending an individual high-risk or high-value case to a reinsurer for customized risk assessment and underwriting approval.
The measured duration, usually in business days, required to complete steps in the underwriting process.
The sum assured limit below which policies can be accepted and issued based purely on health declarations without clinical tests.
An optional policy rider providing supplementary payout in the event of death resulting from an accident.
An optional policy rider that provides a lump-sum payment upon the diagnosis of a contractually specified major medical condition.
The core administration software platform where policies are created, updated, and managed.
The workflow design environment used to map, configure, and manage business processes.
The secure infrastructure layer through which the workflow platform communicates with external systems.
The technical governance committee responsible for reviewing and approving integration patterns and infrastructure additions.
The initial administrative task of inputting physical or digital application details into the workflow system.
The formal entry phase where new applications are logged and registered in the system.

variants: Tests Ordered; Tests Received; medical evidence
definition: The clinical investigations and laboratory procedures ordered to evaluate the health status of an applicant.
A vital cardiovascular reading recorded during the medical examination.

variants: fasting blood; lipid profile; HbA1c lipid; Serum creatinine
definition: A panel of laboratory blood analyses assessing metabolic, diabetic, lipid, and renal function markers.
note: Includes specific medical tests like fasting blood glucose, lipid profile, HbA1c, and serum creatinine under one laboratory testing umbrella.

definition: An electrical recording of heart activity at rest used to screen for cardiovascular abnormalities.

variants: Application Received; Case Closed; Decision Recorded; Offer Issued; Policy Issued; UW Started; UW Complete; Rating Assessed
definition: The sequence of transactional states that track a life insurance application from intake to policy issuance or closure.
The self-disclosed health questionnaire completed by the applicant regarding their medical history.
The automated software system that calculates risk ratings, extra mortality loading, and final policy premium adjustments.
The unique system-generated alphanumeric key used to track an individual case record across systems.

variants: Financial Details; CA-certified financials; income proof; ITR yr
definition: The legal and financial documentation (such as income proofs, tax returns, and chartered accountant statements) collected to justify the sum assured.
note: 'ITR yr' represents Income Tax Return years, a key financial evidence document in the Indian market.

definition: The executive officer in charge of underwriting philosophy, governance guidelines, and circulars.
The management role responsible for supervising operational metrics, turn-around times, and case routing.

variants: Individual Term Life; Individual Life; term life
definition: A class of life insurance product providing pure protection coverage for a defined term of years to an individual policyholder.
A chronic medical condition of insulin resistance frequently evaluated using HbA1c tests during underwriting.
Occupational roles such as flight crew or merchant marine crew that present increased risk profiles and require special rating adjustments.
A disclosure of hereditary illnesses among an applicant's immediate family members used to assess genetic predisposition to certain risks.
An increased body mass index or physical measurements indicating elevated risk due to overweight or obesity.
An underwriting approach where non-standard, complex, or high-risk applications are evaluated manually outside structured grids.

variants: CUO circular; controlled document; guidance note; Training Manual; Underwriter Training
definition: The official documentation, circulars, and manuals that instruct underwriters on standard rules, medical grids, and limits.
Fictional case data created to safely test integration processes and workflow rules without exposing real customer information.

variants: Systems Data; Data stage; data points
definition: The digital data elements and attributes transmitted through core integration staging areas between systems.

variants: Endpoint Method Purpose; GET Retrieve; POST Record
definition: The specific technical API paths and request types used to transfer underwriting details.
The reference premium tables used to determine base pricing based on age, gender, smoker status, and health.
The additional percentage or flat cost added to the base premium to compensate for substandard risks like medical or occupational hazards.
A unit of currency representation equal to 10 million Indian Rupees, used to define major sum assured thresholds.
note: A specific Indian numerical unit commonly encountered in financial and regulatory limits in Indian insurance documents.

definition: The final document or screen that compiles the underwriting decision and justification before a case is officially completed.
The exposure level of the underwritten policy relative to standard pricing assumptions.
The orchestration platform that routes tasks, coordinates status transitions, and interfaces with back-end policy systems.
A medical rating category that assigns a designated level of extra mortality loading to an applicant.
note: Class II is an industry standard rating category indicating mild to moderate extra mortality.

definition: A financial categorization for policies whose face value exceeds standard administrative limits, triggering mandatory medical requirements.
